module_title: Setting Up Your Facebook Reselling Presence

lessons.title: Creating a Facebook Business Page
lessons.body: A Facebook Business Page is your shop's home on Facebook. It looks professional, lets you run ads, and gives customers a single place to see all your products. To create one, go to facebook.com/pages/create. Choose a category like 'Product/Service' or 'Local Business'. For the name, use your business name, e.g., 'Amina's Fabrics Lagos'. If you don't have a name yet, use your own name plus what you sell, like 'Kofi Electronics Accra'. Pick a username that's easy to remember, like @AminasFabrics. Add a profile picture: a clear photo of you or your logo. For the cover photo, use a collage of your best products. In the 'About' section, write what you sell, your location, and how to order. Include your WhatsApp number and mobile money details (e.g., MTN MoMo, M-Pesa). Set your page's call-to-action button to 'Send WhatsApp Message' or 'Shop Now'. Post at least 3 products with clear photos and prices. Use Facebook's scheduling tool to post regularly. Invite your friends to like the page. Share your page link in WhatsApp groups and on other social media. Engage with comments quickly. A Business Page builds trust and makes it easy for customers to find you. It's free and essential for serious reselling.

lessons.title: Joining and Posting in Buy/Sell/Trade Groups
lessons.body: Buy/Sell/Trade (BST) groups are where millions of Africans buy and sell daily. To find them, search Facebook for your city plus 'buy and sell', e.g., 'Lagos Buy and Sell' or 'Nairobi Buy Sell Trade'. Join 5-10 active groups. Read the group rules firstâsome ban direct links or require price in the post. When posting, follow this formula: 1) Clear photo of the item on a plain background. 2) Title with keywords: 'Brand New Samsung Galaxy A12 - 64GB - Nairobi'. 3) Price in local currency, e.g., 'KSh 15,000'. 4) Condition: new or used. 5) Location: 'Westlands, Nairobi'. 6) Payment methods: 'M-Pesa, cash on delivery'. 7) Your WhatsApp number. Post at peak times: 7-9am, 12-2pm, 7-9pm. Use 3-5 relevant hashtags like #Nairobi #Smartphone. Bump your post by commenting 'Still available' after 24 hours. Respond to comments and DMs fast. Don't spam the same post in many groups at onceâFacebook may flag you. Instead, vary the text slightly. If a group allows, offer a small discount for group members. Track which groups bring sales. Leave groups that are full of scammers or have no engagement. Always meet in public places for cash transactions. BST groups are free and can bring quick sales if you post consistently.

lessons.title: Using Facebook Marketplace Effectively
lessons.body: Facebook Marketplace is a dedicated tab for buying and selling locally. It's free and gets millions of views. To list an item, go to Marketplace, click 'Create New Listing', then 'Item for Sale'. Add up to 10 photosâthe first photo is key. Use natural light, show the item from different angles, and include a photo with a ruler or coin for scale. Write a title with brand, model, and key feature: 'HP Pavilion 15 Laptop - 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD'. Set the price competitively. Check similar listings first. Choose the right category and condition. Add a description with details: dimensions, age, reason for selling, any defects. Set your location to your city or neighborhood. Enable 'Messenger' for inquiries. Marketplace shows your listing to people nearby. To boost sales, renew your listing every few days by editing and saving. Share your listing to your timeline and relevant BST groups. Respond to 'Is this still available?' quicklyâwithin an hour if possible. Be ready to negotiate. Meet buyers in safe, public places like malls or police stations. Use cash or instant mobile money transfer. After a sale, mark the item as 'Sold' to avoid wasted messages. You can also create a 'Shop' on Marketplace if you have many items. Marketplace is ideal for bulky items like furniture, electronics, and vehicles. Use it alongside your Business Page for maximum reach.

lessons.title: Writing Compelling Product Descriptions
lessons.body: A good product description answers questions before they're asked and convinces the buyer to act. Start with a benefit-driven headline: 'Stay Cool All Day: Rechargeable Fan with 8-Hour Battery'. Then list key features in bullet points: '3 speeds', 'USB charging', 'quiet motor'. Use sensory words: 'soft cotton', 'sleek design', 'crisp sound'. Include dimensions and weight: '30cm tall, 1.2kg'. State what's included: '1 fan, 1 USB cable, 1 manual'. Mention condition: 'Brand new, sealed' or 'Gently used, no scratches'. Add social proof if possible: 'Over 50 sold this month'. Address common objections: 'No need for electricityâworks on battery'. Use urgency: 'Only 3 left at this price'. End with a clear call to action: 'Message me on WhatsApp 08012345678 to order'. Keep paragraphs short. Use emojis sparingly to break text: â ð¦ ð. Write in simple English. Avoid jargon. If you sell fashion, include size chart: 'S: bust 34in, M: bust 36in'. For electronics, include warranty: '6-month warranty'. Use keywords buyers search: 'original', 'authentic', 'cheap', 'affordable'. Test different descriptions and see which gets more messages. Save templates for similar items. A strong description reduces back-and-forth and builds trust. Always proofread for spelling and grammar. A professional description makes you look reliable and increases sales.

lessons.title: Pricing Strategies for Facebook Sales
lessons.body: Pricing right is key to selling fast and making profit. First, calculate your costs: product cost, transport, packaging, and any fees (e.g., mobile money charges). Add your desired profit margin. For reselling, a 20-50% markup is common. Check competitors on Facebook Marketplace and BST groups. If similar items sell for 10,000, don't price at 15,000 unless you offer extra value. Use psychological pricing: 9,999 instead of 10,000. Offer bundle deals: 'Buy 2 get 10% off'. For new items, price slightly higher to allow negotiation room. For used items, price 30-50% less than new. Consider offering free delivery within your city to justify a slightly higher price. Run flash sales: 'Today only: 20% off'. Use 'anchor pricing': show original price crossed out and your price next to it. For high-demand items, you can price higher. For slow movers, drop price by 10% each week. Accept mobile money, cash, and bank transfer. Factor in delivery costs if you offer it. Don't compete only on priceâcompete on service, speed, and trust. Track your sales to see what price points work. Adjust based on demand. If you get many inquiries but no sales, your price is too high. If you sell out instantly, your price is too low. Test different prices on different groups. Always be transparent about what's included. A fair price builds repeat customers.

lessons.title: Handling Facebook Messenger Inquiries
lessons.body: Most Facebook sales happen in Messenger. How you handle inquiries determines if you close the sale. Respond quicklyâwithin 5 minutes if possible. Set up a saved reply for common questions: 'Hi! Thanks for your interest. The item is available. Price is 15,000. Delivery in Lagos is 2,000. Payment via transfer or cash on delivery. Which would you prefer?' Use a friendly tone. Address the person by name if visible. Answer questions clearly and honestly. If an item is sold, say so immediately and suggest alternatives. For price negotiations, don't drop too fast. Say, 'I can do 14,000 if you pick up today.' If they hesitate, ask what their budget is. Offer a payment plan for expensive items: 'Pay 50% now, 50% on delivery.' Share more photos or videos if requested. Use voice notes for detailed explanations. Always confirm order details: item, price, delivery address, and payment method. Send a payment request via mobile money or bank details. After payment, send a confirmation message and estimated delivery time. Keep the chat professionalâavoid arguments. If someone is rude, stay calm. Use Messenger's 'Away' mode when you're unavailable. Save customer contacts for follow-up. After delivery, ask for a review and offer a discount on next purchase. Good communication turns inquiries into sales and builds a loyal customer base.

quiz.q: What is the first step to create a Facebook Business Page?
quiz.explanation: The correct starting point is the official page creation URL.

quiz.q: Which of these is a recommended category for a reselling Business Page?
quiz.explanation: Product/Service is ideal for resellers as it describes what you sell.

quiz.q: What should you include in the 'About' section of your Business Page?
options: B) Your WhatsApp number and mobile money details
quiz.explanation: Including contact and payment details helps customers order easily.

quiz.q: Why is a Facebook Business Page important for resellers?
options: A) It builds trust and centralizes products
B) It automatically gives you free ads
D) It limits who can see your posts
quiz.explanation: A Business Page looks professional and lets customers see all your offerings in one place.

quiz.q: How many products should you post on your new Business Page to start?
quiz.explanation: Posting at least 3 products shows you are active and gives customers options.

quiz.q: What is a Buy/Sell/Trade (BST) group on Facebook?
options: A) A group for sharing memes
B) A group where people buy and sell items locally
C) A group for job postings
D) A group for political discussion
quiz.explanation: BST groups are specifically for local buying and selling.

quiz.q: How many BST groups should you join initially?
quiz.explanation: Joining 5-10 active groups gives good reach without being overwhelming.

quiz.q: What should you do before posting in a BST group?
quiz.explanation: Reading rules prevents your post from being removed or you being banned.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT recommended in a BST post?
options: C) Spamming the same post in many groups at once
quiz.explanation: Spamming can get you flagged by Facebook; vary your posts instead.

quiz.q: What is a good time to post in BST groups?
quiz.explanation: These are peak engagement times when most people check Facebook.

quiz.q: How can you bump your BST post?
quiz.explanation: Commenting bumps the post to the top of the group feed.

quiz.q: What should you do if a BST group is full of scammers?
quiz.explanation: Leaving unproductive groups saves time and reduces risk.

quiz.q: Where do you create a new listing on Facebook Marketplace?
options: B) In the Marketplace tab, click 'Create New Listing'
quiz.explanation: Marketplace has a dedicated button for creating listings.

quiz.q: How many photos can you add to a Marketplace listing?
quiz.explanation: You can add up to 10 photos, and the first one is most important.

quiz.q: What does renewing a Marketplace listing do?
options: B) Boosts it to the top of search results
quiz.explanation: Renewing (by editing and saving) refreshes the listing so it appears higher.

quiz.q: What is a safe meeting place for Marketplace transactions?
options: B) A public place like a mall or police station
quiz.explanation: Public places reduce safety risks for both parties.

quiz.q: What should you do after selling an item on Marketplace?
quiz.explanation: Marking as sold prevents wasted inquiries and shows you are reliable.

quiz.q: What is a benefit-driven headline for a product description?
options: B) 'Stay Cool All Day: Rechargeable Fan with 8-Hour Battery'
quiz.explanation: It highlights the benefit (stay cool) and key feature (8-hour battery).

quiz.q: Why should you include dimensions and weight in a product description?
options: B) To answer common questions and reduce back-and-forth
quiz.explanation: Buyers want to know size and weight before purchasing, especially for shipping.

quiz.q: What is a good way to address common objections in a description?
options: B) State 'No need for electricityâworks on battery'
quiz.explanation: Directly addressing a concern (like power) builds confidence.

quiz.q: What should you include at the end of a product description?
options: B) A clear call to action
quiz.explanation: A call to action tells the buyer exactly what to do next.

quiz.q: Why use emojis in product descriptions?
options: B) To break up text and make it visually appealing
quiz.explanation: Emojis can make descriptions easier to scan and more engaging.

quiz.q: What is a common markup for reselling?
quiz.explanation: A 20-50% markup is typical to cover costs and make profit.

quiz.q: What is psychological pricing?
quiz.explanation: 9,999 seems significantly lower than 10,000 to many buyers.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get many inquiries but no sales?
quiz.explanation: High interest but no sales often means the price is too high.

quiz.q: What is anchor pricing?
options: A) Showing original price crossed out next to your price
B) Pricing at the lowest possible
quiz.explanation: Anchor pricing makes your price look like a better deal.

quiz.q: Why should you track your sales?
options: A) To see what price points work
quiz.explanation: Tracking helps you adjust pricing based on demand.

quiz.q: What is the recommended response time for Messenger inquiries?
quiz.explanation: Fast responses increase the chance of closing the sale.

quiz.q: What should you do if an item is sold?
options: B) Say it's sold and suggest alternatives
quiz.explanation: Honesty and offering alternatives can still lead to a sale.

quiz.q: What is a good way to handle price negotiations in Messenger?
options: B) Say 'I can do 14,000 if you pick up today'
quiz.explanation: Conditional discounts encourage quick action without giving away too much.
